name: io.github.2016judea/classic-literature
title: Classic Literature
description: Emotional arcs, influence chains, prose look-alikes and genres of classic novels, from full texts

tools.name: novel_mood_arc
tools.description: For 'what is the emotional arc of X', 'does X end happier or sadder than it begins', 'where does X turn', 'which novels feel like X as they go'. Sentiment of the full Gutenberg text of 339 classic novels (1678-1928), scored in 100 parts and smoothed: start, end, the change and its rank among all 339, the shape by thirds (Rise, Fall, Rise–fall, Fall–rise), where the sharpest turn falls, the arc every 10%, and the 5 novels whose arcs correlate most closely. Fuzzy-matches the title; if the novel is not in the corpus it says so and lists the closest titles.

title.description: The novel's title, e.g. 'Moby-Dick', 'Pride and Prejudice'

author.description: Optional author, to pick between similar titles

full_arc.description: true = also return all 100 points of the smoothed arc

tools.name: writers_who_sound_like
tools.description: For 'who writes like X', 'which authors sound like X', 'who is closest to X in style / in ideas'. Over 77 writers from Homer to Joyce: nearest by distinctive vocabulary (TF-IDF) and nearest by ideas and imagery (embeddings), plus the writer's prose circle. For Cormac McCarthy, Herman Melville and William Shakespeare it adds the character-GPT cross-reading: a small GPT trained on each one reading the others (bits per character), each author's word tells, and which book a model's generated text lands nearest.

limit.description: How many nearest writers per measure (default 8)

tools.name: influence_chain
tools.description: For 'how is X connected to Y', 'did X influence Y', 'trace the influence from X to Y'. Shortest chain of documented influence links (Wikidata 'influenced by' plus model-attested) through 77 authors, each link with its direction, source and how alike the two authors' texts are. Says plainly when no chain exists or an author is not in the network.

tools.name: author_influences
tools.description: For 'who influenced X', 'who did X influence', 'X's literary influences'. Documented influences in and out for one of 77 authors, ranked by conceptual similarity of their texts, with sources, the author's influence circle and how connected they are.

tools.name: genre_of_book
tools.description: For 'what genre is X by its prose', 'which genre does X belong to', 'what genres did Y write in'. Genres recovered from the words alone across 345 pre-1929 novels: the cluster's name, size, span, distinctive words and held-out library label, the novels nearest in time in the same cluster, and when the genre's name caught on where a name clock exists. Pass a title, or an author for all their novels.

author.description: An author: alone for all their novels, or with title to disambiguate

tools.name: genre_history
tools.description: For 'when did detective fiction emerge', 'when did people start saying "Gothic novel"', 'is mystery fiction just detective fiction renamed', 'what genres are there'. The prose cluster (when it first forms, its novels, earliest and latest) and the genre-name clock from Google Books (first attested, the years it reached 10% and half of its mentions, the peak, mentions per billion words every 20 years). Leave genre empty to list every genre and clock.

genre.description: A genre or its name, e.g. 'detective fiction', 'gothic novel', 'sea story', 'western'. Empty = list all.

tools.name: books_like
tools.description:
Novels in this corpus most like a given one, two measured ways: the same genre by the novel's own prose (nearest in year) and the emotional arcs that move most alike, plus the ones that are alike both ways. Over 345 pre-1929 novels.

Example questions:
- "Books like Dracula"
- "If I loved Jane Eyre, what should I read next?"
- "Novels similar to The Count of Monte Cristo"

author.description: Optional author, to pick between similar titles

tools.name: does_book_have_a_happy_ending
tools.description:
A one-line verdict on whether a novel ends happier or sadder than it begins, from the sentiment of its full text, then the full arc reading (start, end, change and its rank, shape, sharpest turn, alike novels). 339 novels scored, 1678-1928.

Example questions:
- "Does Great Expectations have a happy ending?"
- "Is Tess of the d'Urbervilles sad?"
- "How does Wuthering Heights end, emotionally?"

tools.name: saddest_and_happiest_novels
tools.description:
Classic novels ranked by the sentiment of their full text: overall mood, mood of the ending, or how far the mood moves from first page to last. Optional year range. 339 novels scored, 1678-1928.

Example questions:
- "What is the saddest classic novel?"
- "Which Victorian novels have the happiest endings?"
- "Novels that get darker as they go"

measure.description: overall = whole text (default), ending = last 10%, change = end minus start

tools.name: novels_by_author
tools.description:
Every novel by one author in this corpus, in order of year, with the genre its prose places it in and how the author's novels split across genres.

Example questions:
- "What novels did Charles Dickens write?"
- "Which Jane Austen books are covered?"
- "Did Walter Scott write in more than one genre?"

tools.name: classic_novels_from_era
tools.description:
The novels in this corpus from a year range and/or a prose genre, oldest first, with each one's genre, how many match by genre, and whether its arc was scored. Corpus: 345 pre-1929 novels.

Example questions:
- "Classic novels from the 1840s"
- "Detective novels written before 1900"
- "What sea stories were published between 1850 and 1900?"

genre.description: Optional prose genre, e.g. 'Detective fiction', 'sea story', 'Historical romance'

tools.name: did_author_influence
tools.description:
A yes/no answer on whether one author influenced another: a direct documented link, a link running the other way, or the chain that connects them, then each link with its sources. 77 authors.

Example questions:
- "Did Poe influence Arthur Conan Doyle?"
- "Was Melville influenced by Shakespeare?"
- "Did Dostoevsky read Dickens?"

from_author.description: The possible influence, e.g. 'Edgar Allan Poe'

to_author.description: The possibly influenced author, e.g. 'Arthur Conan Doyle'

tools.name: what_genres_are_there
tools.description:
The genres recovered from the prose of 345 pre-1929 novels (size, span, when each cluster first forms) and the genre names tracked through Google Books (when each caught on).

Example questions:
- "What genres did 19th-century novels fall into?"
- "When did the word 'western' catch on?"
